newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish court rejects Maastricht documents request.
newsitem.headline: Danish court rejects Maastricht documents request.

text.p: A Danish citizens' group challenging the legality of their country's European Union membership suffered a setback on Friday when court authorities turned down its request to have confidential government documents brought in evidence.

"The procedural committee did not find that the request was a matter of sufficient principle to warrant allowing the 11 citizens' lawyers to appeal to the Supreme Court against the High Court's recent rejection of their demands," procedural committee chairman Hans Kardal told the Ritzau news agency.

The rebuff followed a preliminary High Court hearing to set the boundaries for a legal challenge by the non-partisan Constitution Committee which says that since joining the EU in 1973 Denmark has ceded national authority to European institutions in breach of the constitution.
Limiting the scope of the trial, expected to begin in earnest next year, is seen by legal experts as strengthening the government's prospects of a victory.
Defeat could oblige it to renegotiate its EU treaties from scratch or seek to amend the constitution, a tortuous process requiring a general election and a referendum.
Danes have a history of coolness towards the EU.

They rejected Maastricht altogether in a 1992 referendum and approved it the following year only on condition that Denmark stay out of European Monetary Union and joint defence, policing and citizenship arrangements.
